It compared the efficacy and safety of two dose schedules of pacritinib in pooled and individual arm analyses versus BAT in subjects with thrombocytopenia and primary myelofibrosis (PMF), post-polycythemia vera MF or post-essential thrombocythemia MF.

endpoint.text: Two coprimary endpoints at Week 24: proportion of patients with ≥35% spleen volume reduction (SVR) by MRI/CT, and proportion with ≥50% reduction in Total Symptom Score (TSS).

citations.quote: PERSIST-2 had two coprimary efficacy endpoints at Week 24: The proportion of patients with SVR \ge 35\% and the proportion of patients with \ge 50\% reduction in the TSS. The trial was successful on the SVR endpoint but not on the TSS endpoint.

n.text: 311 patients randomized 1:1:1 (pacritinib 400 mg QD n=104, pacritinib 200 mg BID n=107, BAT n=100).

citations.quote: A total of 311 patients was randomized 1:1:1 to receive oral pacritinib 400 mg QD (104 [33.4%] patients), pacritinib 200 mg BID (107 [34.4%] patients), or investigator-determined BAT (100 [32.2%] patients).

result.text: SVR ≥35% at Week 24 (ITT Efficacy population): pacritinib 200 mg BID 16/74 (21.6%) vs BAT 2/72 (2.8%), p=0.0007. The TSS coprimary endpoint was not met: pooled pacritinib 37/149 (24.8%) vs BAT 10/72 (13.9%), p=0.08.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>20%) are diarrhea (48% vs 15%), thrombocytopenia (34% vs 23%), nausea (32% vs 11%), anemia (24% vs 15%), and peripheral edema (20% vs 15%). Most common serious adverse reactions were anemia (8% vs 3%), thrombocytopenia (6% vs 2%), cardiac failure (4% vs 3%), and pyrexia (4% vs 2%).
